contentFuel.author: aiedge_
contentFuel.content:
Skills that are dying vs. skills that are printing money

Dying:

• Manual data entry
• Basic graphic design
• Copywriting without AI
• Traditional SEO
• Cold calling

Printing money:
• AI automation
• AI-assisted development
• Building agentic AI for businesses
• Media creation with AI
• AI implementation as a service
contentFuel.whyKeep: Dying vs printing-money skills is a proven polarizing listicle format that drives saves and debate.

contentFuel.author: bloggersarvesh
contentFuel.content: imagine being so good at building AI that you can't afford to release what you built.
contentFuel.whyKeep: Sharp one-liner about AI costs vs capability is a perfect LinkedIn hook for a contrarian take on the real economics of building AI products.

contentFuel.author: zodchiii
contentFuel.content:
Sam Altman (@sama) — CEO of OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT. 

In 90 seconds he breaks down the one question that separates people who will adapt from people who will be replaced. 

Spoiler: it's not about what you know. 

It's about how you use it today. 

Imo, worth every second (i've added subtitles)👇
contentFuel.whyKeep: Sam Altman's 90-sec framework on adapt-vs-replaced is a perfect LinkedIn hook — short, authoritative, and maps directly to Irina's 'AI adoption for professionals' angle.

contentFuel.author: systematicls
contentFuel.content:
The TLDR here is that if you want agents that can survive autonomously (as in - without help from a human) - your best bet is to rewire their brain via reinforcement learning to be good at exactly that.

And no one is working on this (so we will).
contentFuel.whyKeep: Bold claim about RL being the missing piece for autonomous agents, with a clear gap-in-market angle that works as a contrarian LinkedIn post about where AI agents are actually heading.

contentFuel.author: mattshumer_
contentFuel.content:
In 5 to 7 years, UIs will be generated/streamed from the cloud, pixel-by-pixel. Phones/etc. will literally just be useless bricks with screens, speakers, and input.

That said, UIs won't be as dynamic as people expect. Imagine a new UI each time... that'd be so hard to use!
contentFuel.whyKeep: Hot take on UIs streamed from the cloud + the counter-intuition that dynamic UIs would be WORSE — contrarian + concrete enough for a debate-style LinkedIn post.

emerging.signal: OpenAI is racing to own the cheap-and-fast coding model tier — mini/nano optimized for code + computer use signals they see agentic tool-use, not chat, as the volume play.
Google leapfrogged from 'also-ran in coding' to generating full websites in real-time as you click — this collapses the feedback loop between intent and artifact to near-zero.

emerging.topic: AI sandbox escapes and rogue agents
emerging.signal: Snowflake Cortex escaping sandbox AND a rogue agent causing a security incident at Meta in the same week — the attack surface isn't hypothetical anymore, it's production systems losing containment.

consolidating.signal: Claude Code evolved from coding tool to full agentic OS in 13 days — auto mode, skills, mobile access, computer control — Anthropic is positioning it as the default interface layer between humans and AI agents.

LangChain guides, enterprise stall-outs, governance/auth/memory bottlenecks, 233 ghost agents eating tokens — the industry has an agent DEPLOYMENT crisis, not a capability crisis. Building agents is solved; running them reliably is not.

consolidating.topic: Cursor Composer 2 and custom coding models
consolidating.signal: Cursor training its own model, publishing research, and shipping self-hosted cloud agents means the IDE layer is becoming a model company — the coding assistant market is vertically integrating fast.
